blocks.text: SINGAPORE — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said on Saturday Filipinos are now more concerned with getting cheaper electricity than with where it comes from, suggesting a shift in public attitudes toward nuclear energy despite longstanding safety concerns. Marcos said public concerns about nuclear safety appeared to be giving way to demands for more affordable electricity. “Because we always worry about, people are worried about safety and the answer that comes back is that we don’t care where our power comes from, but bring it more cheaper.
